payload.title: vmsfs/vmsrms: fix missing function, infinite recursion, thread safety
payload.context:
## Critical bugs in filesystem stack

### F1. rms_parse.c:16,76 — vmsfs_resolve() does not exist
`extern int vmsfs_resolve(...)` declared and called at line 76 but function does not exist in codebase. sys$parse will fail to link or crash.

**Fix:** Either implement vmsfs_resolve() or replace the call with the correct existing function (likely vmsfs_to_linux_path or similar).

### F7. vmsfs_translate.c:398-406 — infinite recursion in vmsfs_resolve_device()
Circular logical names (A→B:, B→A:) cause unbounded recursion → stack overflow.

**Fix:** Add depth counter parameter, fail after MAX_DEPTH (e.g., 10) with SS$_TOOMANYLNAM.

### F11. lnm_daemon.c:87-213 — no thread safety in LNM daemon
Spawns pthread per client (line 384) but lnm_manager_t and lnm_table_t hash tables have no mutex. Concurrent CREATE/DELETE/TRANSLATE corrupt hash chains.

**Fix:** Add rwlock to lnm_manager. Read lock for TRANSLATE, write lock for CREATE/DELETE.

### F21. vmsfs_device.c:20-24 — device table is unprotected global
Accessed from multiple threads with no synchronization.

**Fix:** Add mutex around device_table access.

### F6. rms_core.c:571-574 — duplicate IFI counters
sys$open uses `static uint16_t next_ifi = 1`, sys$create uses `static uint16_t create_ifi = 1`. IFI values can collide.

**Fix:** Use a single shared static counter for both.

## Key files
- src/vmsrms/rms_parse.c (line 16, 76)
- src/vmsfs/vmsfs_translate.c (vmsfs_resolve_device, line 398)
- src/vmslnm/lnm_daemon.c (thread safety)
- src/vmsfs/vmsfs_device.c (device table)
- src/vmsrms/rms_core.c (IFI counters, lines 571-574)

## Done condition
- sys$parse links and works (vmsfs_resolve exists or replaced)
- Circular logical names detected and error returned
- LNM daemon safe under concurrent access
- Device table access synchronized
- IFI values never collide between open and create
- All tests pass

payload.title: vmsrms: fix B-tree trust, version lookup, protection, unchecked I/O
payload.context:
## High/medium bugs in Record Management Services

### F4. rms_idx.c:461-462 — btree accepts untrusted num_keys from file
marker value from .rms_idx file assigned directly to node->num_keys without bounds check. Corrupted file can cause OOB writes into node->keys[], key_lens[], offsets[].

**Fix:** Validate: `if (marker > BTREE_MAX_KEYS) return -EINVAL;`

### F2. rms_core.c:157-170 — double-dot in versioned file lookup
rms_next_version passes dot-prefixed extension (".txt") to vmsfs_get_highest_version which already adds a dot. Search pattern becomes "name..txt;N".

**Fix:** Strip leading dot from ext before passing: `const char *ext_no_dot = (dot[0] == '.') ? dot + 1 : dot;`

### F5. rms_idx.c:551-555 — btree_load ignores fread returns
Five fread calls for tree metadata discard return values. Truncated file → uninitialized values.

**Fix:** Check each fread return == 1. Return error if not.

### F9. rms_core.c:903 — sys$display stores raw st_mode instead of VMS protection
Stores Unix permission bits in xab$w_pro. Should call vmsfs_mode_to_protection (already declared extern at line 29).

**Fix:** `pro->xab$w_pro = vmsfs_mode_to_protection(st.st_mode);`

### F10. rms_core.c:902 — sys$display stores only st_uid, losing group
VMS UIC is (group<<16)|member. Currently only stores uid.

**Fix:** `pro->xab$l_uic = ((uint32_t)(st.st_gid & 0xFFFF) << 16) | (uint32_t)(st.st_uid & 0xFFFF);`

### F8. vmsfs_version.c:230-251 — TOCTOU race in create_new_version
Scans for highest version, creates N+1 with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, retries once on EEXIST. Insufficient under concurrency.

**Fix:** Loop retry until success or non-EEXIST error, with bounded retry count.

### F16. rms_core.c:634 — O_TRUNC specified twice in sys$create
Always includes O_TRUNC, then adds it again if FAB$M_SUP. Second add is dead code.

**Fix:** Only add O_TRUNC when FAB$M_SUP is set.

### F17. rms_core.c:660-666 — pre-allocation overflow
`size_t total = cell_size * fab->fab$l_mrn` can overflow.

**Fix:** Check for overflow before multiplication.

### F18. rms_idx.c:433-446 — btree_write_node ignores fwrite returns
**Fix:** Check returns, propagate errors.

### F20. rms_core.c:462 — save_metadata ignores fwrite return
**Fix:** Check return.

### F24. rms_seq/rel/idx — triplicated read_exact/write_exact
Three identical implementations across rms_seq.c, rms_rel.c, rms_idx.c.

**Fix:** Move to shared rms_util.c or rms_core.c.

## Key files
- src/vmsrms/rms_idx.c, rms_core.c, rms_parse.c, rms_seq.c, rms_rel.c

## Done condition
- B-tree validates num_keys from disk
- Version lookup produces correct filenames
- sys$display returns VMS protection format
- fread/fwrite returns checked throughout
- All tests pass

payload.title: DCL: fix unchecked fwrite, editor overflow, dead code from split

## DCL shell bugs and cleanup

### D1. dcl_backup.c:158,180-182,188 — unchecked fwrite in BACKUP save
All fwrite calls writing to saveset silently discard return values. Partial write → corrupt .BCK file.

### D2. dcl_library.c:115,357-359 — unchecked fwrite in LIBRARY
Same pattern in create/insert. Also D3: ftell() at line 204 and 234 can return -1, cast to malloc size wraps to huge allocation.

### D4. dcl_cmd_file.c:450,1088 — unchecked fwrite in COPY and APPEND
Partial writes (disk full) silently truncate output.

### D5. dcl_terminal.c:235 — unchecked fwrite in terminal table save

**Fix for D1-D5:** Check fwrite return == expected count. On failure, report VMS error (RMS$_WER or similar), close file, return error status.

### D6. dcl_editor.c:372 — strcpy overflow in EDT substitution
`strcpy(result + prefix_len + new_len, found + old_len)` into result[EDT_MAX_LINE*2] without checking combined length.

**Fix:** Calculate total length first, check against sizeof(result), truncate or error if too long.

### D7. dcl_cmd_process.c:354,402 — atol for user entry IDs
No error detection on non-numeric input.
**Fix:** Use strtol with endptr checking.

### D8. dcl_cmd_file.c:481 — atol in PURGE version parsing
Same issue.
**Fix:** strtol with validation.

**Fix:** Check ftell >= 0 before using as size.

### D10. dcl_cmd_show.c:119-145 — dead tables[] struct
Unused struct array silenced with (void)tables. Leftover scaffolding.
**Fix:** Remove entirely.

dcl_cmd_io.c:431 has RUN comment (function is in dcl_cmd_process.c).
dcl_cmd_io.c:57-60 has DIFFERENCES comment (function is in dcl_cmd_misc.c).
dcl_cmd_misc.c has multiple orphaned section headers.
dcl_cmd_process.c:1060 has "External Utility Executor" header for function in dcl_cmd_misc.c.

payload.context:
## Bugs in the boot orchestrator

### I1. ovmx_init.c:166 — unchecked write() in copy_recursive
Primary file-copy path for system installation. Partial writes produce corrupt files.
**Fix:** Check write return, retry or error.

### I2. ovmx_init.c:114 — unchecked finit_module return
Kernel module loading failure silently ignored. Boot continues with no kernel module support.
**Fix:** Check return, print error message if module fails to load.

### I3. ovmx_init.c:141-143 — path truncation in copy_recursive
512-byte buffers with snprintf. Deep directory trees silently truncate paths.
**Fix:** Check snprintf return against buffer size, skip/warn on truncation.

### I4. vmssshd.c:603-606 — double waitpid race
SIGCHLD handler can reap child, then blocking waitpid on line 606 hangs or the WNOHANG on 594 reaps first.
**Fix:** Only waitpid once, with WNOHANG, in a loop. Or set a flag in SIGCHLD handler and check it.

### I5. vmssshd.c:493, vms_login.c:109 — localtime NULL deref
**Fix:** Check localtime return for NULL.

### I6. vms_authorize.c:55 — duplicate sysuaf_record_t definition
Defined both locally and in system header sysuaf.h. Can diverge.
**Fix:** Remove local definition, use sysuaf.h.

### I7. vms_sysman.c:238-258 — 128KB stack buffer
`char lines[256][512]` in cmd_startup_remove.
**Fix:** malloc or reduce buffer size.

## Key files
- src/ovmx_init/ovmx_init.c
- src/vmsssh/vmssshd.c
- tools/vms_login.c, vms_authorize.c, vms_sysman.c

payload.title: Kernel: fix status code collision, buffer overflow, metadata flush
payload.context:
## Kernel data integrity and correctness bugs

### K14. vms_internal.h — SS__INSFMEM and SS__BADPARAM both 0x00000014
```c
#define SS__BADPARAM    0x00000014
#define SS__INSFMEM     0x00000014  /* same value! */
```
Code checking for one matches the other. One must be changed. Check real VMS values: SS$_BADPARAM=0x14 (20), SS$_INSFMEM=0x02C (44).

**Fix:** Change SS__INSFMEM to 0x0000002C (44) to match VMS. Grep all .c files in src/kernel/ for SS__INSFMEM usage to verify no behavioral change.

### K18. vmsfs_blkdev.c:729-730 — buffer overflow writing directory entries
```c
de->de_name_len = name_len;
memcpy(de->de_name, name, name_len);  // de_name is 80 bytes
```
`name_len` comes from `strlen(base)` (line 1311) bounded by VMSFS_MAX_FILENAME (85). 85 > 80 = overflow.

**Fix:** Clamp `name_len` to `sizeof(de->de_name) - 1` before memcpy. Also add validation at the caller.

### K19. vmsfs_blkdev.c:620 — block allocations not flushed to disk
`vmsfs_ensure_blocks()` updates inode i_blocks and retrieval pointers in memory only. Caller `vmsfs_get_block` (line 115) does not call `vmsfs_blkdev_flush_inode()`. Crash after alloc but before next explicit flush = lost mapping = data corruption.

**Fix:** Call `vmsfs_blkdev_flush_inode()` after successful `vmsfs_ensure_blocks()` in `vmsfs_get_block`.

### K11. vmsfs_blkdev.c:1065-1072 — readdir position accounting broken
Free slots (de_fid==0) skipped without incrementing entry_pos. Position becomes unstable if entries deleted between readdir calls — entries skipped or emitted twice.

**Fix:** Always increment entry_pos regardless of whether slot is free. Free slots are counted for position but not emitted.

## Key files
- src/kernel/vms_internal.h (status codes)
- src/kernel/vmsfs/vmsfs_blkdev.c (buffer overflow, flush, readdir)

## Done condition
- SS__INSFMEM != SS__BADPARAM
- name_len clamped before memcpy into de_name
- Block allocations flushed to disk immediately
- readdir stable across concurrent deletes
- Kernel builds, QEMU tests pass

payload.title: Kernel: fix remaining medium/low issues (races, leaks, locking)
payload.context:
## Kernel medium and low severity issues

### K4. vms_lock.c:66-73 — unchecked kmem_cache_create returns
`vms_lock_cache` and `vms_resource_cache` can be NULL if alloc fails. Subsequent kmem_cache_zalloc will NULL deref.
**Fix:** Check returns, propagate error from vms_lock_init (change return type to int).

### K6. vms_module.c:66-76 — TOCTOU race in vms_proc_register
Check-if-exists and insert are not atomic. Two threads with same PID can both insert.
**Fix:** Move the existence check inside the spinlock-protected section.

### K8. vms_eflag.c:219 — data race on *flags in wait_event condition
After dropping spinlock, flags accessed without synchronization.
**Fix:** Use READ_ONCE() in the wait_event condition.

### K9. vms_eflag.c:393-404 — inconsistent lock ordering (proc->ef.lock vs vms_common_ef_lock)
Different acquisition orders in ascefc vs dacefc.
**Fix:** Document and enforce consistent ordering: always proc->ef.lock first, then vms_common_ef_lock.

### K10. vms_lock.c:184 — GFP_ATOMIC in process context
resource_find_or_create uses GFP_ATOMIC unnecessarily in ioctl (process context).
**Fix:** Drop spinlock, alloc with GFP_KERNEL, re-acquire and re-check.

### K12. vms_lock.c:101-120 — lock_find_by_id returns unprotected pointer
Concurrent vms_proc_release_locks could free the lock between find and use.
**Fix:** Add refcount to lock entries, or hold lock across find+use.

### K13. vms_lock.c:82-94 — cleanup only frees resources, leaks lock entries
**Fix:** Iterate each resource granted/waiting list and free lock entries before freeing resource.

### K15. vmsfs_blkdev.c:101 — integer overflow in VBN conversion
sector_t can be 64-bit, cast to uint32_t truncates.
**Fix:** Validate block < UINT32_MAX before conversion.

### K16. vmsfs_file.c:135-142 — f_pos race in concurrent I/O
Swapping iocb->ki_filp and f_pos not protected.
**Fix:** Use inode mutex or per-file lock around f_pos manipulation.

### K17. vmsfs_version.c:224 — dentry_open with NULL mnt (dead code)
**Fix:** Remove the dead code path or properly populate dir_path.mnt.

### K20. vms_ast.c:42 — local SS__INSFMEM redefinition
Multiple .c files redefine status codes locally. Risk of divergence.
**Fix:** Remove local #defines, use vms_internal.h exclusively.

### K21. vmsfs_blkdev.c:1373 — FID leak on alloc_block failure in mkdir
**Fix:** Free the FID before returning error.

### K22. vms_module.c:256-259 — dev_release does not clean up process state
Crashed processes leak their vms_proc entry permanently.
**Fix:** Call vms_proc_free in vms_dev_release.

## Key files
- src/kernel/vms_lock.c, vms_module.c, vms_ast.c, vms_eflag.c
- src/kernel/vmsfs/vmsfs_blkdev.c, vmsfs_file.c, vmsfs_version.c

## Done condition
- All issues addressed, kernel builds, QEMU tests pass

payload.title: Security: fix command injection and privilege escalation in tools
payload.context:
## Security vulnerabilities in VMS tools

### T1. vms_tcpip_config.c:86-88 — command injection via system()
`run_tcpip_cmd()` passes user-provided strings (IP addresses, domain names) into system() via shell. Single quotes in input break the shell command. Input like '; rm -rf /; echo ' executes arbitrary commands.

**Fix:** Replace system() with fork/exec pattern (like dcl_exec_utility). Pass arguments directly, no shell interpretation. Or at minimum, sanitize input to reject shell metacharacters.

### T2. vms_authorize.c:692-709 — privilege check via environment variable
check_privilege() reads VMS_PRIVILEGES env var. Any user can `export VMS_PRIVILEGES=ALL` and run AUTHORIZE to modify SYSUAF. Also line 704: strstr(buf, "ALL") matches substrings.

**Fix:** Do not use environment variables for privilege checking. Read the calling user's privileges from the PCB or from SYSUAF directly. For the substring issue, use word-boundary matching or exact comparison against known privilege names.

### T3-related. vms_sysman.c:196-198 — system() usage
cmd_startup_add calls system(mkdircmd). Not currently exploitable (compile-time constant), but system() is a dangerous pattern.

**Fix:** Replace with mkdir() syscall directly.

## Key files
- tools/vms_tcpip_config.c (run_tcpip_cmd, lines 80-90)
- tools/vms_authorize.c (check_privilege, lines 692-709)
- tools/vms_sysman.c (cmd_startup_add, line 196)

## Done condition
- No system() calls with user-provided data
- Privilege checks do not rely on environment variables
- All tools build and pass tests

payload.title: Tools: fix vms_mail bugs (SYSUAF delimiter, stack overflow, off-by-one)
payload.context:
## vms_mail.c has multiple critical bugs

### T3a. vms_mail.c:138,183 — wrong SYSUAF delimiter
user_exists() and get_user_homedir() use strchr(line, ':') but SYSUAF uses pipe ('|') as delimiter (confirmed in vms_authorize.c:148 and ovmx_init.c:484-487). User lookup is completely broken — mail SEND validation never finds any user.

**Fix:** Change colon delimiter to pipe in both functions.

### T3b. vms_mail.c:366,373 — 3.8MB stack allocations
```c
mail_entry_t save_msgs[MAX_MESSAGES];    // MAX_MESSAGES=9999, ~384 bytes each = ~3.8MB
mail_entry_t recip_msgs[MAX_MESSAGES];   // another ~3.8MB
```
Guaranteed stack overflow on any platform with default stack size.

**Fix:** malloc these arrays, or reduce MAX_MESSAGES significantly, or use a different approach (dont copy all messages to filter).

### T3c. vms_mail.c:408 — off-by-one array write
`&recip_msgs[recip_msg_count]` when recip_msg_count==MAX_MESSAGES writes past array bounds. No bounds check.

**Fix:** Add bounds check before appending.

### T3d. vms_mail.c:74 — 3.8MB static array
`mail_entry_t g_messages[MAX_MESSAGES]` is ~3.8MB of static data.

**Fix:** Reduce MAX_MESSAGES to a sane default (e.g., 1000) or allocate dynamically.

### T3e. vms_mail.c:772-792 — overly permissive abbreviation matching
strncmp(verb, "HELP", 1) matches anything starting with H. strncmp(verb, "QUIT", 1) matches anything starting with Q.

**Fix:** Use minimum-uniqueness matching consistent with DCL conventions (at least 2-3 chars).

## Key files
- tools/vms_mail.c

## Done condition
- SYSUAF parsed with pipe delimiter
- No stack allocations > 64KB
- Bounds checks on array writes
- Build succeeds, basic mail commands work

payload.title: Tools: fix vms_analyze bitmap inversion, vms_sysman header, vms_help overflow
payload.context:
## Bugs in analysis and system management tools

### T5. vms_analyze.c:135 — bitmap free-block counter inverted
Code counts SET bits as "free", but INITIALIZE (vms_initialize.c:128-129) SETS bits to mark blocks as ALLOCATED. So bitmap_free actually counts allocated blocks. The comparison `if (bitmap_free != hb.hb_free_blocks)` will always report INCONSISTENT on a valid volume.

**Fix:** Invert the counting: free blocks are CLEAR bits (bit == 0), not SET bits.

### T6. vms_sysman.c:323 — reads sysparams.dat without header
cmd_parameters_show() calls fread(&param, sizeof(param), 1, fp) directly from file start. But sysgen_params.h wraps params in struct sysgen_file with magic, version, and count header fields. First read parses header bytes as a parameter → garbage output. Same issue in cmd_parameters_set() at line 386.

**Fix:** Read and validate the sysgen_file header first (check magic, version), then read count params.

### T7. vms_help.c:480 — stack overflow on deep navigation
stack[depth] = strdup(input) with no depth check against MAX_DEPTH (9). Navigating >9 levels writes past stack[] array.

**Fix:** Add `if (depth >= MAX_DEPTH) { print error; continue; }` before the strdup.

### T8. vms_help.c:511-515 — SYS$HELP env var used without VMS path translation
`snprintf(full_path, ..., "%s/HELPLIB.HLP", env_path)` uses forward-slash Linux join on what might be a VMS directory spec.

**Fix:** If env_path contains VMS filespec (brackets, colons), translate via vmsfs_to_linux_path first.

## Key files
- tools/vms_analyze.c (lines 130-140)
- tools/vms_sysman.c (lines 320-390)
- tools/vms_sysgen.c (sysgen_params.h for header format)
- tools/vms_help.c (lines 475-515)

## Done condition
- ANALYZE reports correct free block count on a valid volume
- SYSMAN PARAMETERS SHOW reads params correctly after header
- HELP does not crash on deep navigation
- All tools build

payload.title: libvms: fix pointer truncation, use-after-free, string overflows
payload.context:
## Critical memory safety bugs in libvms

### L14-15. lib_misc.c:238,254 — lib$find_file truncates 64-bit pointer to uint32
```c
*context = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)pglob;          // line 238: truncates pointer
pglob = (glob_t *)(uintptr_t)(*context);          // line 254: reconstructs wrong address
```
On 64-bit systems, the upper 32 bits of the glob_t* are lost. Every subsequent call uses a wrong pointer → crash or corruption.

**Fix:** Change context type to uintptr_t or uint64_t. Or store glob_t* in a side table indexed by a uint32 handle.

### L10. lib_vm.c:419-425 — use-after-free in lib$delete_vm_zone
```c
munmap((void *)ext, ext->size);
ext = ext->next;    // ext was just unmapped!
```
**Fix:** Save ext->next before munmap: `next = ext->next; munmap(...); ext = next;`

### L16. str_routines.c:74 — str$concat uint16 overflow → buffer overflow
```c
uint16_t total = src1->dsc$w_length + src2->dsc$w_length;  // wraps if both near 65535
```
Then memcpy copies full lengths into undersized allocation.
Same pattern in L17 str$prefix (line 436) and L18 str$append (line 472).

**Fix:** Check for overflow before allocating: if (src1->dsc$w_length + src2->dsc$w_length > 65535) return STR$_STRTOOLON. Use uint32 for the intermediate sum.

### L11. sys_lock.c:130 — path injection in lock file name
```c
snprintf(lockpath, ..., "%s/%s.lck", LOCK_DIR, name);
```
Resource name from user descriptor with no sanitization. "../" in name creates files outside LOCK_DIR.

**Fix:** Reject names containing "/" or ".." characters. Or hash the name for the filename.

### L19. sys_operator.c:52 — localtime() NULL deref
```c
struct tm *tm = localtime(&ts.tv_sec);  // can return NULL
```
Then immediately dereferences tm->tm_mday.

**Fix:** Check for NULL return, use a fallback if NULL.

## Key files
- src/libvms/rtl/lib_misc.c (lib$find_file context handling)
- src/libvms/rtl/lib_vm.c (lib$delete_vm_zone)
- src/libvms/rtl/str_routines.c (str$concat/prefix/append)
- src/libvms/syssvc/sys_lock.c (lock file path)
- src/libvms/syssvc/sys_operator.c (localtime)

## Done condition
- lib$find_file works on 64-bit (no pointer truncation)
- lib$delete_vm_zone does not access freed memory
- str$ routines reject overflow instead of wrapping
- Lock file names sanitized
- No NULL deref on localtime failure
- All tests pass

payload.title: libvms: fix FAO varargs UB, stack overflow, IOSB truncation
payload.context:
## High severity bugs in libvms system services and RTL

### L3. sys_fao.c:282 — 64KB stack buffer
`char temp_buf[FAO_MAX_INTERNAL_BUF]` (65536 bytes) on stack. Stack overflow risk in threaded contexts.

**Fix:** malloc the buffer, or reduce FAO_MAX_INTERNAL_BUF and check for truncation.

### L4. sys_fao.c:359-371 — sys$fao reads uninitialized varargs
Reads up to 64 uint64_t values from va_arg regardless of how many the caller passed. UB.

**Fix:** FAO directives should drive argument consumption. Count directives in the control string to know how many args to read. Or document that callers must pass exactly the right number of args (VMS convention).

### L5. lib_datetime.c:186-200 — lib$sys_fao same varargs UB
Same pattern: reads 64 uint64_t regardless of actual arg count.

**Fix:** Same approach as L4.

### L6-7. lib_signal.c:121-129,231-236 — lib$signal/lib$stop varargs UB
Reads up to 29 uint32_t, stopping at first zero. Zero-termination heuristic fails if a legitimate argument is zero.

**Fix:** Use condition value argument count field (STS$V_ARGS in condition value) to determine argument count per VMS convention, or require explicit count parameter.

### L9. sys_qio.c:84 — IOSB byte count truncated to uint16
```c
iosb->iosb$w_bcnt = (uint16_t)result;
```
I/O returning >65535 bytes silently loses high bits. Same issue in sys_uring.c:231.

**Fix:** For large I/O, use the extended IOSB field (iosb$l_dev_depend has 32-bit space per iosbdef.h). Or document the 64KB limit.

### L8. sys_uring.c:137 — memset clears completions during re-init
If called while I/O is in flight, active completion slots are zeroed.

**Fix:** Only initialize if uring_fd is not already valid. Add a guard.

### A9. lib_datetime.c:213-214 — type-pun cast uint32_t* to uint64_t*
```c
return sys$faol(ctrl_str, outlen, out_str, (const uint64_t *)prmlst);
```
Reads 8 bytes for each 4-byte argument.

payload.title: PLAN: VMS image activation — IMGACT.EXE, shareable images, INSTALL, system disk install
payload.context:
Replace Unix dynamic linking with VMS-native image activation.

## Objective
QEMU boots from system disk with dynamically linked VMS executables, shareable images in SYS$LIBRARY, OVMX own image activator (IMGACT.EXE as ELF PT_INTERP, not ld.so), INSTALL utility for known images, GSMATCH version checking, and a real VMS-style installation experience. No glibc. No Unix dynamic linker visible.

## Architecture
IMGACT.EXE is a static musl binary registered as the ELF interpreter (PT_INTERP). The Linux kernel loads it automatically on exec(). It replaces ld-musl/ld-linux.

Only two binaries are static: STARTUP.EXE (PID 1) and IMGACT.EXE (image activator). Everything else is dynamically linked against shareable images via IMGACT.EXE.

Shareable images are musl-linked ELF shared objects with VMS metadata in custom ELF sections (.vms.ident for GSMATCH). Symbol resolution uses standard ELF relocations (RELATIVE, JUMP_SLOT, GLOB_DAT, TLSDESC) — activation is controlled by our code, not the system dynamic linker.

INSTALL utility manages the Known Image Database. IMGACT.EXE checks this first before searching SYS$SHARE.

## Key Design Decisions
- IMGACT.EXE statically includes musl libc and exports its symbols (same design as musl libc.so which IS ld-musl)
- Symbol vectors (replacing PLT/GOT) are NOT feasible without compiler changes — explicit non-goal
- Hardcoded fallback search path before VMSLNMD starts (chicken-and-egg resolution)
- Docker path stays on glibc for now; IMGACT.EXE is QEMU-only initially
- aarch64 first, x86_64 second

## Full design spec: docs/design-image-activation.md (child bead 1)

payload.title: Design spec: docs/design-image-activation.md
payload.context:
Write the full design specification for VMS image activation in OVMX.

## Deliverable
docs/design-image-activation.md — the authoritative reference for all implementation beads.

## Required Sections

### 1. Image Activator Architecture
- IMGACT.EXE as static musl binary, registered as ELF interpreter via PT_INTERP
- Kernel loads IMGACT.EXE on exec(), IMGACT.EXE loads the target executable and dependencies
- IMGACT.EXE statically includes musl libc and exports its symbols to loaded images
- Same design as musl libc.so (which IS ld-musl — single binary is both libc and dynamic linker)

### 2. Activation Sequence (step-by-step)
1. Kernel loads IMGACT.EXE, passes executable info via auxv
2. IMGACT.EXE opens executable, reads ELF headers
3. mmaps executable LOAD segments
4. Parses DT_NEEDED entries for shareable image dependencies
5. For each dependency: search known image DB → SYS$SHARE path → RPATH
6. Recursively load all dependencies (topological sort)
7. Process ELF relocations: R_AARCH64_RELATIVE, JUMP_SLOT, GLOB_DAT, TLSDESC
8. Initialize TLS (thread control block, TLS blocks for __thread variables)
9. Call INIT/INIT_ARRAY constructors in dependency order
10. Transfer control to executable entry point

### 3. Shareable Image Format
- Standard ELF shared objects built with musl-gcc
- VMS metadata in custom ELF sections:
  - .vms.ident: image name, GSMATCH operator (LEQUAL/EQUAL/ALWAYS), major.minor version, link timestamp
  - .vms.imgid: image identification (linker version, build host, etc.)
- SONAME set to VMS name (LIBVMS$SHR.EXE)
- Standard PLT/GOT (compiler generates these — cannot replace without compiler changes)

### 4. Search Path Resolution
- Priority order: Known Image Database → hardcoded SYS$SHARE (/vms/SYS0/SYSCOMMON/SYSLIB) → RPATH
- Hardcoded fallback necessary before VMSLNMD starts (chicken-and-egg)
- After VMSLNMD: resolve SYS$SHARE logical name for search
- RPATH from ELF binary as last resort

### 5. GSMATCH Version Checking
- Shareable images carry .vms.ident with GSMATCH operator + major.minor
- Executables record the version they were linked against
- At activation: compare linked version vs actual version per operator
- LEQUAL: actual >= linked (default, allows newer)
- EQUAL: exact match required
- ALWAYS: any version accepted
- Mismatch → %IMGACT-F-GSMATCH error

### 6. INSTALL Utility and Known Image Database
- INSTALL ADD/LIST/REMOVE commands
- Known Image Database: VMS$KNOWN_IMAGES.DAT in SYS$SYSTEM
- Loaded into memory by IMGACT.EXE at first activation
- O(1) lookup by SONAME (hash table)
- /OPEN: pre-opened file descriptor cached
- /SHARED: mmap(MAP_SHARED) gives automatic physical page sharing (Linux kernel handles this)
- /HEADER_RESIDENT: header data cached in memory
- Rebuilt every boot by SYSTARTUP_VMS.COM

### 7. Boot Sequence with Image Activation
- STARTUP.EXE (static, PID 1) — boots, mounts disk, runs SYSTARTUP_VMS.COM
- SYSTARTUP_VMS.COM — INSTALL ADD for each shareable image, start daemons
- First exec() after disk mount → kernel loads IMGACT.EXE from SYS$SYSTEM
- All subsequent processes activated through IMGACT.EXE

### 8. Build System Changes
- OVMX_IMGACT=ON cmake option
- musl-gcc for all targets
- Executables: -Wl,--dynamic-linker=/vms/SYS0/SYSCOMMON/SYSEXE/IMGACT.EXE
- STARTUP.EXE and IMGACT.EXE: always static
- Fix __getauxval symbol issue (weak alias)

### 9. System Disk Installation
- Fat initramfs: STARTUP.EXE + IMGACT.EXE (static) + all dynamic binaries + shareable images
- First boot: detect blank disk → create dirs → copy files → write SYSTARTUP_VMS.COM → reboot
- Installed disk has real files (no symlinks)
- Slim initramfs: STARTUP.EXE only, everything else from disk

### 10. TLS Handling Strategy
- Our code uses __thread in: vms_pcb.c, dcl_messages.c, lib_signal.c, vms_kif.c
- 3 TLSDESC relocations across 2 libraries (LIBVMS$SHR.EXE, LIBVMSPROCESS$SHR.EXE)
- IMGACT.EXE must set up thread control block and allocate TLS blocks
- Architecture-specific: aarch64 uses TPIDR_EL0 register, x86_64 uses FS segment

### 11. Explicit Non-Goals
- Symbol vectors replacing PLT/GOT (requires compiler changes)
- dlopen/dlsym/LIB$FIND_IMAGE_SYMBOL (phase 2)
- Privileged shareable images (CHMK/CHME)
- Docker unification (Docker stays glibc)
- PCSI package manager
- Lazy binding (VMS resolves all symbols at activation)

## Done Condition
Document exists at docs/design-image-activation.md, covers all 11 sections above, reviewed for accuracy against the codebase and the design discussion.

payload.title: IMGACT.EXE — core image activator (aarch64)
payload.context:
Build the VMS image activator as a static musl binary that serves as ELF interpreter.

## What IMGACT.EXE Does
Static musl binary at /vms/SYS0/SYSCOMMON/SYSEXE/IMGACT.EXE. The Linux kernel loads it when any OVMX executable is exec()d (via PT_INTERP in the ELF header).

## Implementation

### Entry Point
IMGACT.EXE receives control from the kernel with:
- Stack: argc, argv, envp, auxv (standard ELF interpreter ABI)
- auxv contains AT_PHDR, AT_PHENT, AT_PHNUM, AT_ENTRY, AT_BASE for the target executable
- AT_EXECFN contains the executable path

### Activation Steps
1. Parse auxv to find target executable info
2. If not already mapped by kernel, open and mmap the executable LOAD segments
3. Parse the executable dynamic section (DT_NEEDED, DT_RELA, DT_JMPREL, etc.)
4. For each DT_NEEDED entry:
   a. Search known image cache (shared memory segment, populated by INSTALL)
   b. Search hardcoded path: /vms/SYS0/SYSCOMMON/SYSLIB/
   c. Search DT_RPATH/DT_RUNPATH from the executable
   d. If not found: %IMGACT-F-IMGNOTFND error, exit
5. Open and mmap each shareable image, recursively resolve its DT_NEEDED
6. Topological sort all loaded images (dependency order)
7. For each image (leaves first):
   - Process R_AARCH64_RELATIVE relocations (simple base address adjustment)
   - Process R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT relocations (resolve symbol, store address in GOT)
   - Process R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT relocations (resolve symbol, store in PLT GOT)
   - Process R_AARCH64_TLSDESC relocations (set up TLS descriptor)
8. Initialize TLS:
   - Calculate total TLS size across all modules
   - Allocate TLS block (thread control block + TLS data)
   - Set TPIDR_EL0 register to point to TCB
   - Copy TLS initialization images
9. Call INIT functions, then INIT_ARRAY functions (dependency order, leaves first)
10. Jump to executable entry point (AT_ENTRY from auxv)

### Symbol Resolution
- Build hash table from each image DT_SYMTAB + DT_HASH/DT_GNU_HASH
- Resolve symbols by searching: executable → loaded images in order → IMGACT.EXE own symbols
- IMGACT.EXE exports musl libc symbols (it statically includes musl libc)
- The __getauxval symbol: provide weak alias to getauxval

### Error Reporting
- %IMGACT-F-IMGNOTFND, image not found: <name>
- %IMGACT-F-GSMATCH, image version mismatch: <name> (stub for now, full impl in GSMATCH bead)
- %IMGACT-F-RELOCERR, relocation error at <addr>
- %IMGACT-F-TLSERR, TLS initialization failed

### Build
- Source: src/imgact/imgact.c (+ arch-specific: src/imgact/arch/aarch64/)
- Static musl: musl-gcc -static
- Must NOT depend on any OVMX library (it IS the foundation)
- Approximate size: 800KB-1MB (includes musl libc)

### Key Files to Study
- musl ldso/dynlink.c (MIT license) — reference implementation for ELF loading
- Our binaries use only 3 relocation types + TLSDESC (verified via readelf)
- 344 symbols exported by LIBVMS$SHR.EXE, 171 imported by DCL.EXE

## Done Condition
A test program linked with -Wl,--dynamic-linker=/vms/.../IMGACT.EXE that depends on a test shareable image:
1. Kernel loads IMGACT.EXE
2. IMGACT.EXE finds and maps the shareable image from /vms/.../SYSLIB/
3. Relocations processed, symbols resolved
4. Test program runs and calls functions from the shareable image
5. TLS variables work (__thread int x = 42; assert(x == 42))
6. VMS error message printed if shareable image not found

Does NOT need to boot full OVMX — just prove the activation mechanism works with a minimal test case.

payload.title: GSMATCH version checking in IMGACT.EXE and post-link tooling
payload.context:
Add VMS image version checking to the activation path.

## Components

### Post-Link Tool: vms_imgident
Adds .vms.ident ELF section to shareable images. Can be a standalone C tool or cmake custom command using objcopy.

Section contents (binary struct):
- magic: "VMSI" (4 bytes)
- image_name: char[32]
- gsmatch_op: uint8 (0=LEQUAL, 1=EQUAL, 2=ALWAYS)
- major_version: uint16
- minor_version: uint16
- link_timestamp: uint64 (Unix epoch)

### CMake Integration
After linking each shareable image, run vms_imgident to stamp the .vms.ident section. Version comes from cmake variables (per-library or global).

### IMGACT.EXE Changes
At activation time, for each DT_NEEDED shareable image:
1. Read .vms.ident from the loaded shareable image
2. Read the recorded dependency version from the executable (stored in a .vms.deps section added at link time)
3. Compare per GSMATCH operator
4. On mismatch: %IMGACT-F-GSMATCH, image <name> version <actual> incompatible with required <linked> (operator <op>)

### ANALYZE/IMAGE Enhancement
ANALYZE/IMAGE command (tools/vms_analyze.c) reads and displays .vms.ident sections:
- Image name, version, link timestamp
- GSMATCH operator and version

## Done Condition
1. Build LIBVMS$SHR.EXE with GSMATCH LEQUAL,1,5
2. Link DCL.EXE against it (records version 1.5 dependency)
3. Replace LIBVMS$SHR.EXE with version 1.3 → activation fails with %IMGACT-F-GSMATCH
4. Replace with version 1.7 → activation succeeds (LEQUAL: 1.7 >= 1.5)
5. ANALYZE/IMAGE shows version info

payload.title: INSTALL utility — known image database and IMGACT.EXE integration
payload.context:
Implement the INSTALL utility for managing known (pre-registered) images.

## INSTALL Command
External utility at SYS$SYSTEM:INSTALL.EXE (or DCL builtin). Subcommands:

INSTALL ADD SYS$SHARE:LIBVMS$SHR.EXE /OPEN /SHARED /HEADER_RESIDENT
INSTALL LIST [/FULL]
INSTALL REMOVE SYS$SHARE:LIBVMS$SHR.EXE

### Qualifiers
- /OPEN: mark file as pre-opened (IMGACT.EXE keeps fd cached)
- /SHARED: mark for shared memory mapping (MAP_SHARED — Linux kernel shares physical pages automatically for read-only segments)
- /HEADER_RESIDENT: cache ELF headers in memory (skip disk read on activation)

### Known Image Database
File: SYS$SYSTEM:VMS$KNOWN_IMAGES.DAT
Format: binary file with fixed-size records:
- image_name: char[64] (SONAME)
- image_path: char[256] (resolved filesystem path)
- flags: uint32 (OPEN|SHARED|HEADER_RESIDENT)
- gsmatch: version info (cached from .vms.ident)

Loaded into shared memory segment at boot (or first INSTALL ADD). IMGACT.EXE reads this segment for O(1) lookup by SONAME before doing filesystem search.

### IPC Between INSTALL and IMGACT.EXE
Options:
a) Shared memory (mmap of the .DAT file with MAP_SHARED) — simplest
b) Unix domain socket to a daemon — more complex but supports notifications
c) File-based with IMGACT.EXE re-reading on activation — simplest, slightly slower

Recommend (a): IMGACT.EXE mmaps VMS$KNOWN_IMAGES.DAT at startup. INSTALL writes to same file. Changes visible immediately via shared mapping.

### SYSTARTUP_VMS.COM Integration
Boot script includes:
$ INSTALL ADD SYS$SHARE:LIBVMS$SHR.EXE /OPEN /SHARED /HEADER_RESIDENT
$ INSTALL ADD SYS$SHARE:LIBVMSPROCESS$SHR.EXE /OPEN /SHARED
$ INSTALL ADD SYS$SHARE:LIBVMSFS$SHR.EXE /OPEN /SHARED
... etc for each shareable image

## Done Condition
1. INSTALL ADD registers an image, INSTALL LIST shows it
2. IMGACT.EXE finds known images without filesystem search
3. INSTALL REMOVE de-registers, IMGACT.EXE falls back to filesystem
4. Multiple processes running DCL share physical pages for LIBVMS$SHR.EXE code (verify via /proc/PID/smaps or similar)

## Changes to STARTUP.EXE (src/ovmx_init/ovmx_init.c)

### Installation Path
When is_system_installed() returns false (blank disk):
1. Create ODS-2 directory structure (existing provision_dirs — extend if needed)
2. Copy IMGACT.EXE to SYS$SYSTEM (critical — must be first, before any exec)
3. Copy all shareable images to SYS$LIBRARY (real files, not symlinks)
4. Copy all executables to SYS$SYSTEM (real files, not symlinks)
5. Copy config files to SYS$MANAGER (STARTUP.COM, SYLOGICALS.CONF, etc.)

8. Generate SYSTARTUP_VMS.COM with INSTALL ADD commands for each shareable image
9. Provision users from SYSUAF (existing provision_sysuaf_users)

The current provision_symlinks() creates symlinks from SYSEXE → /usr/local/bin. This is the Docker path only. For QEMU/IMGACT mode, we copy real files. The symlink path can remain for Docker compatibility but should not be used when dynamic binaries are available in the initramfs.

$ ! SYSTARTUP_VMS.COM — Generated by STARTUP.EXE installation

payload.title: make install-disk build target
payload.context:
PLAN: Clean install architecture — eliminate Docker-mode contamination, unify install path, produce system disk image.

## Problem
Runtime code (DCL, SSH, ovmx_init) has Docker-mode assumptions leaked in: hardcoded /usr/local/bin fallbacks, symlink machinery, two separate install codepaths. The real system uses vmsfs on a block device. Docker is a convenience layer and should not poison runtime design.

## Contamination points
1. dcl_exec_utility() in dcl_cmd_misc.c:380-386 — hardcodes /usr/local/bin fallback
2. vmssshd.c:51 — OVMX_BIN_DIR="/usr/local/bin", DCL_SHELL_PATH derives from it
3. ovmx_init.c:78-87 — bin_search_dirs/lib_search_dirs scan Linux paths
4. install_system() vs install_system_blkdev() — two separate install functions
5. ensure_vms_binary/ensure_vms_library — symlink provisioning machinery
6. is_system_installed() checks "file or symlink"

## Desired end state
- Runtime code (DCL, SSH) only knows VMS paths: SYS$SYSTEM, SYS$LIBRARY
- Dockerfile puts binaries directly at VMS paths (/vms/SYS0/SYSCOMMON/SYSEXE/), no /usr/local/bin intermediary
- One install codepath in ovmx_init (not two)
- Build produces system.dsk (pre-installed vmsfs disk image) as artifact
- QEMU first-boot with blank disk still works (INITIALIZE + install from initramfs)

payload.title: Build produces system.dsk — pre-installed vmsfs disk image
payload.context:
Build produces system.dsk — pre-installed vmsfs disk image.

## Approach
Boot QEMU headless with kernel + initramfs + blank disk. Init already does INITIALIZE + install_system_blkdev (copies all files onto mounted vmsfs). Shut down. The disk IS the artifact.

Steps for the build:
1. qemu-img create -f raw system.dsk 256M
2. Boot QEMU headless: qemu-system-x86_64 -nographic -kernel vmlinuz -initrd initramfs.cpio.gz -drive file=system.dsk,format=raw,if=virtio -append "console=ttyS0 quiet" 
3. Init runs: load vmsfs.ko → detect blank /dev/vda → INITIALIZE → mount → copy_recursive (install) → boot → shutdown
4. Need an auto-shutdown mechanism: init should detect "install-only" mode (kernel cmdline param?) and halt after install instead of launching SSH/login
5. Output: system.dsk with OVMX installed

## What to build
- Add kernel cmdline option: ovmx.install_only=1 — init installs then halts
- Add Dockerfile.bootable stage or script that runs QEMU to produce the disk
- Or standalone script: distro/make-disk.sh

payload.title: Dockerfile.bootable update for disk boot
payload.context:
Update Dockerfile.bootable to produce both initramfs AND system disk image. QEMU launches with both.

## Current State
- Dockerfile.bootable (128 lines) produces vmlinuz + initramfs-ovmx.cpio.gz
- No system disk image produced
- run-qemu.sh accepts optional DISK env var but no disk is built

## What to Change
- Add install-disk step to Dockerfile.bootable after initramfs creation
- Output: vmlinuz, initramfs-ovmx.cpio.gz, AND system.dsk
- Update run-qemu.sh to auto-detect system.dsk in output directory and pass as -drive
- Preserve initramfs-only mode when no disk present (vms-whi fallback)

## Key Files
- Dockerfile.bootable (add disk image build step)
- distro/boot/run-qemu.sh (auto-detect disk)
- vms-p78 (install-disk target, dependency)

## Done Condition
- `docker build -f Dockerfile.bootable -o dist .` produces all three artifacts
- `run-qemu.sh dist/vmlinuz dist/initramfs-ovmx.cpio.gz` boots with system disk
- System disk contains full OVMX installation

payload.title: Fallback boot to initramfs
payload.context:
If no system disk found at boot, fall back to initramfs-only mode with VMS warning message.

## Current State
- ovmx_init.c (lines 200-264) already has partial fallback logic:
  - Checks /dev/vda (SYSDISK_DEV) for block device
  - If present and formatted, mounts to /vms
  - If mount fails, backs up initramfs to /tmp/initramfs_vms and uses overlay mode (vmsfs backing=/var/vmsfs)
- No VMS-style warning message printed on fallback

## What to Change
- Print VMS-format warning: %%BOOT-W-NOSYSDISK, no system disk found, booting from initramfs
- Ensure all services (LNMD, DCL, SSH) work in initramfs-only mode
- Verify overlay mode properly layers initramfs content
- Test: boot QEMU without -drive flag → system comes up in initramfs mode with warning

## Key Files
- src/ovmx_init/ovmx_init.c (boot orchestrator, disk detection logic)
- distro/boot/run-qemu.sh (QEMU launcher, optional DISK parameter)

## Done Condition
- QEMU boot without system disk prints %%BOOT-W-NOSYSDISK warning and boots successfully
- All basic functionality works in initramfs-only mode (login, DCL, logical names)
- QEMU boot WITH system disk still works normally (no regression)

payload.title: Rightslist integration into access checks
payload.context:
Wire RIGHTSLIST.DAT into VMS access control checks.

## Current State
- RIGHTSLIST.DAT exists at distro/rootfs/vms/SYS0/SYSCOMMON/SYSEXE/RIGHTSLIST.DAT
- Format: IDENTIFIER:VALUE:ATTRIBUTES (INTERACTIVE:1:RESOURCE, BATCH:2:RESOURCE, etc.)
- Not referenced in any access control code (no imports in src/)
- sys$check_access exists in sys_security.c but does not consult rights database
- vms.ko kernel module has access check hooks but no rights integration

## What to Change
- Load RIGHTSLIST.DAT at boot (parse into in-memory rights table)
- sys$check_access: consult rights table when checking process rights
- Process rights: each process inherits rights from SYSUAF account (DEFPRIVILEGES + identifiers)
- vms.ko: export rights check interface for kernel-level file protection
- SHOW PROCESS/RIGHTS displays process held identifiers

## Key Files
- distro/rootfs/vms/SYS0/SYSCOMMON/SYSEXE/RIGHTSLIST.DAT (data file)
- src/libvms/syssvc/sys_security.c (sys$check_access)
- src/kernel/vms_access.c (kernel access checks)
- src/libvms/syssvc/sys_uai.c (load user rights at login)

## Done Condition
- Rights loaded from RIGHTSLIST.DAT at boot
- sys$check_access considers held identifiers
- AUTHORIZE GRANT/REVOKE modifies rights database
- SHOW PROCESS/RIGHTS displays held identifiers
